title: Using a library from its header
description:
The starter contains `tinyini`, a small configuration library like the one in lesson 4.03. It has no web page: everything you need is in its **doc comments**. Do not change the library; read it, and use it to write `loadSettings`.

```cpp-norun
struct ServerSettings { std::string host; int port; bool tls; int workers; };
std::optional<ServerSettings> loadSettings(std::string_view text, std::string& error);
```

`loadSettings` reads a configuration text and checks it in this order, stopping at the first problem. On a problem it returns an empty optional and sets `error` to the message shown; on success it sets `error` to an empty string.

| Setting | Rule | Message |
|---|---|---|
| the text | must parse | `line N`, where N is the malformed line |
| `[server] host` | optional, default `localhost`; if present it must not be empty | `bad server.host` |
| `[server] port` | **required** | `missing server.port` |
| | a whole number from 1 to 65535 | `bad server.port` |
| `[server] tls` | optional, default false; if present it must be a boolean the library understands | `bad server.tls` |
| `[pool] size` | optional, default 4; if present a whole number from 1 to 256 | `bad pool.size` |

Notice that two messages for the port need you to tell "missing" from "not a number". Read what the library's functions return in each case.
hints: `findInt` and `findBool` return an empty optional both for a missing key and for a bad value, as their comments say. Call `find` first: it returns null only when the key is missing.
Work through the table from top to bottom, returning at the first problem. Start from the defaults and overwrite each one only when its key is present and valid.
